question: Where can I get a list of active mines and quarries in the United States, with location, mineral or rock extracted, operator and annual production?

answer.summary: MSHA's weekly Mines file is the national list: 6,671 mines with Active status (6,096 metal/non-metal including stone, sand and gravel; 575 coal) with coordinates, operator, county and primary commodity; 6,492 of them reported work hours in 2025. Annual production per mine is published only for coal (its 2025 total matches EIA's 527.6 million short tons); quarries have hours but no tonnage. Pennsylvania DEP lists tons for 898 noncoal mines (2025).
main_caveats: MSHA 'Active' is a registry status, not proof of extraction: 6,492 of 6,671 Active mines reported hours in 2025, but so did 4,672 Intermittent and 745 Abandoned mines.
MSHA ANNUAL_COAL_PROD holds coal only; its unit is not in the definition file (its 2025 sum equals EIA's 527.6 million short tons).
Quarry and metal mines appear in the MSHA production file with hours and employees; ANNUAL_COAL_PROD is nonzero in only 113 non-coal rows over 2000-2026.
Pennsylvania repeats the same tonnage across permits of one site and its site rows sum to 103,947,203 tons against a printed total of 103,945,203.
MSHA 'Facility' mines (482 Active) are mills or plants, and 1,171 Active mines are portable operations, so a point may not be the pit.
State registries (CA SMARA, NV) record permit or operator-reported status; California says it cannot guarantee operator-reported coordinates.
answer.confidence_reason: MSHA, Pennsylvania and California files were downloaded and counted and coal totals matched EIA; USGS NMIC and most states were not opened.

attributes.note: MSHA Mines.txt: lat/lon for 6,659 of 6,671 Active mines (mostly 6 decimals); CA DMR 749 active and NV 157 points. Points only, no boundaries.
MSHA PRIMARY_SIC and PRIMARY_CANVASS (e.g. Construction Sand and Gravel, 2,123 active mines); PA 'Mineral'; CA PriProduct; NV COMMODITY.
MSHA CURRENT_OPERATOR_NAME on all 6,671 Active mines (3,561 operator ids) plus controller; CA Operator, PA Company, NV OPERATOR.
Coal: MSHA ANNUAL_COAL_PROD per mine (524 mines in 2024). Noncoal: PA DEP tons for 898 mines (2025); MSHA gives quarries only hours.
attributes.gap_note: No national per-mine tonnage for stone, sand, gravel or metals in MSHA, the CA DMR CSV or the NV layer. USGS NMIC facility data and other states were not opened.

Mine name, state code and county name.
C = coal, M = metal/non-metal (includes stone, sand and gravel).
Facility, Surface or Underground.
Abandoned, Abandoned and Sealed, Active, Intermittent, New Mine, NonProducing or Temporarily Idled, and the date it began.
Latest operator and controlling legal entity.
Primary commodity extracted at the mine (SIC description) and industry group (Stone, SandAndGravel, Nonmetal, Metal, Coal).

how_to_use.example_request: curl -sL -o Mines.zip https://arlweb.msha.gov/OpenGovernmentData/DataSets/Mines.zip  # unzip; read Mines.txt with delimiter '|' and encoding latin-1; keep CURRENT_MINE_STATUS == 'Active'. Production: https://arlweb.msha.gov/OpenGovernmentData/DataSets/MinesProdYearly.zip, sum ANNUAL_COAL_PROD by MINE_ID and CALENDAR_YR.
how_to_use.example_result: Mines.txt: MINE_ID 0100003, O'Neal Quarry & Mill, Surface, Active since 01/22/1979, AL, Shelby, PRIMARY_SIC Lime, PRIMARY_CANVASS Stone, LATITUDE 33.177778, LONGITUDE -86.758889. MinesProdYearly 2025: Oak Grove Mine (0100851) ANNUAL_HRS 925328, ANNUAL_COAL_PROD 2394204.
steps: Download Mines.zip (7,320,580 bytes; Mines.txt 39,432,301 bytes, 92,129 rows) and read it as pipe-delimited Latin-1 text.
Select CURRENT_MINE_STATUS == 'Active' (6,671 rows) and, to require recent work, join MinesProdYearly on MINE_ID and keep mines with ANNUAL_HRS > 0 in the latest full year.
Take position from LATITUDE and LONGITUDE (6,659 Active rows have both); treat PORTABLE_OPERATION == 'Y' as a base location.
Sum ANNUAL_COAL_PROD over subunits per MINE_ID and CALENDAR_YR for coal output; for non-coal mines use hours and employees only.
Read the definition files (Mines_Definition_File.txt, MineSProdYearly_Definition_File.txt) for field meanings.
reading_traps: 'Active' is a registry status: of 6,671 Active mines, 6,492 reported hours in 2025, while 4,672 Intermittent and 745 Abandoned mines also reported hours.
ANNUAL_COAL_PROD is coal only: nonzero in 27,600 coal rows and in just 113 non-coal rows (2000-2026) whose meaning is undocumented; quarries have hours and employees only.
No unit is given for ANNUAL_COAL_PROD; the 2025 sum is 527,653,155, equal to EIA's 527.6 million short tons, with 473 mines above zero versus EIA's 472.
Production rows are per subunit (underground, surface, mill or plant, shop); a mine has several rows per year and mill rows carry hours but no tonnage.
Active 'Facility' mines (482) are plants or mills, and 1,171 Active mines are portable operations.
The production file names its columns differently from Mines.txt (CALENDAR_YR, C_M_IND, ANNUAL_HRS); 2026 is a partial year (24,590 rows).
16 Active rows with a latitude lie in American Samoa, Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands; some American Samoa rows have a blank longitude.
The open-data page carried a banner that the week's data would be postponed, yet the files were modified on 2026-11-23.

evidence.quote: The Mine dataset lists all Coal and Metal/Non-Metal mines under MSHA's jurisdiction since 1/1/1970. It includes such information as the current status of each mine (Active, Abandoned, NonProducing, etc.), the current owner and operating company, commodity codes and physical attributes of the mine.
Production may not have been reported and may not contain data (null values).
Values are Abandoned, Abandoned and Sealed, Active, Intermittent, New Mine, NonProducing and Temporarily Idled.
Highlights for 2025 U.S. coal production increased 2.9% year over year to 527.6 million short tons (MMst). The number of producing coal mines decreased from 524 to 472 mines.

how_to_use.example_request: curl -sL -O https://files.dep.state.pa.us/Mining/BureauOfMiningPrograms/BMPPortalFiles/Annual_Reports/IndustrialAnnualReports/2025/2025IndustrialMineralsMines_ListedbyCounty.xlsx  # read sheet1: header row 6 (Company, Permit, Site Name, Acres, Production, Mineral, ...), county names in column A
how_to_use.example_result: Adams County, permit 01740601, Gettysburg Quarry, 113 acres, Production 193414, Mineral Hornfels, 47 employees, 9761 hours. Statewide Totals row: 898 mines, 103,945,203 tons.
steps: Download the XLSX (138,500 bytes) and read sheet1.
Keep rows with a permit in column B, a site name in column C and numeric production in column E; drop rows whose column A ends in 'Total' or 'Totals' and repeated header rows.
County is a section header row (e.g. 'Adams County'), not a column: carry it down to the site rows.
reading_traps: County subtotal rows ('<County> Total') and a 'Statewide Totals' row are mixed with site rows; adding every numeric row triple-counts production.
Site rows sum to 103,947,203 tons against the printed total of 103,945,203; the 2,000-ton difference was not reconciled.
Four groups of rows repeat the same company, site and tonnage under different permits (e.g. 193,414 tons shown for both permit 01740601 and 01080301).
The workbook has no coordinates; location is county only, so locating a mine needs the permit or the operator address file.
898 mines reported in 2025 against 603 in 2024 because small noncoal mines were added, so year-on-year counts are not comparable.

how_to_use.example_result: California CSV: 1,977 rows, 749 ACTIVE; example Mine_ID 91-33-0008 CABAZON QUARRY, PriProduct Sand and Gravel. Nevada layer 4: 157 features, fields NAME, OPERATOR, COMMODITY, COUNTY.
steps: California: download the CSV from the DMR All Mines item (721,098 bytes) and keep MineStatus == 'ACTIVE' (749 rows); ReportYear shows how recent each report is.
Nevada: query layer 4 of the ActiveMines MapServer with outSR=4326; the service rejects pagination but returned all 157 features in one call.
To compare with MSHA, match by distance: the ids do not correspond (MSHA 0402774 vs California 91-33-0008).
reading_traps: A SMARA permit or an ACTIVE status is operator-reported and is not proof of extraction; California says it cannot guarantee operator-reported coordinates.
No production field in either layer; California annual reports (MRRC-2) exist but their per-mine tonnage was not found in the CSV.
California status is upper case (ACTIVE 749, RECLAIMED 732, IDLE 100) and a mine can be CLOSED yet still listed.
A 1 km spatial match linked 192 of 302 MSHA California Active mines with a DMR ACTIVE mine; the rest differ in definition (mills, portable plants) or location.

Nevada services of the same name carry several years (2017, 2019, 2021, 2025 layers); the ActiveMines2023 service description still speaks of mines active in 2017. The OPERATOR text of the first record is cut off mid-parenthesis.
